annotations.title: 迪化
annotations.body: 迪化，即今烏魯木齊，為清代新疆重鎮。乾隆朝兩度用兵準噶爾，平定天山南北，展拓西北疆域，並在此設治屯戍。乾隆帝屢言「中外一家」，以天下一家之說統攝內地與藩部，將新疆納入大一統版圖。

zh-Hans.title: 迪化
zh-Hans.body: 迪化，即今乌鲁木齐，为清代新疆重镇。乾隆朝两度用兵准噶尔，平定天山南北，展拓西北疆域，并在此设治屯戍。乾隆帝屡言「中外一家」，以天下一家之说统摄内地与藩部，将新疆纳入大一统版图。

en.title: Dihua
en.body: Dihua (today's Ürümqi) was a key Qing stronghold in Xinjiang. Under the Qianlong emperor, two campaigns against the Dzungars pacified both sides of the Tianshan, expanded the northwest frontier, and established administration and military colonies here. Qianlong often spoke of "one family within and beyond," folding Xinjiang into a unified imperial map of the inner lands and outer dependencies.

annotations.title: 題識
annotations.body:
本朝幅員之廣亘古未有東西南朔莫不紀極而萬國之梯航重譯職貢稱臣者更指不勝屈乾隆
      丁亥年間餘姚黃千人曾為天下輿圖其中山川疆界都邑封圻靡不星羅棋布如指諸掌洵足瞻
盛世之版章為遠近之觀度矣然其時金川西藏新疆州郡未經開闢而河道海口等尚不無挂漏之說
      兹刻遵      御纂諸書悉為增補較舊圖似加詳晰全圖內每方百里凡省■̅府從□廳從▮直隸
      州從⌂州從■縣從●關從⏠營鎮從◎土司從▲其塞徼緜亘無際海峙風設不時雜以里數計
      者其方向俱仍舊式未敢稍易己見舊圖勒石不便攜帶屏幅途寓中玩鑒已加整正博雅君子
      使歸全壁之懸覽幸焉
   嘉慶十有七年歲在壬申桂月上浣吉旦

zh-Hans.title: 题识
zh-Hans.body:
本朝幅员之广亘古未有，东西南朔莫不纪极，而万国之梯航重译、职贡称臣者更指不胜屈。乾隆丁亥年间，余姚黄千人曾为天下舆图，其中山川疆界、都邑封圻靡不星罗棋布、如指诸掌，洵足瞻盛世之版章，为远近之观度矣。然其时金川、西藏、新疆州郡未经开辟，而河道海口等尚不无挂漏之说。兹刻遵      御纂诸书悉为增补，较旧图似加详晰。全图内每方百里；凡省■̅，府从□，厅从▮，直隶州从⌂，州从■，县从●，关从⏠，营镇从◎，土司从▲。其塞徼绵亘无际、海峙风设不时、杂以里数计者，其方向俱仍旧式，未敢稍易己见。旧图勒石不便携带，屏幅途寓中玩鉴已加整正，博雅君子使归全壁之悬览幸焉。
嘉庆十有七年岁在壬申桂月上浣吉旦
（以上为题识原文的现代标点整理；图例符号与御字前空格仍依原刻。）

en.title: Colophon
en.body:
A Jiaqing-era colophon (1812) praises the empire’s unprecedented breadth, and the realms that come by ship and interpreter to offer tribute and acknowledge the throne — more than the fingers can count. It recalls Huang Qianren of Yuyao and his world map of 1767 (Qianlong dinghai): mountains, rivers, boundaries, and seats laid out like points on the palm, truly enough to behold the territorial order of a flourishing age. Jinchuan, Tibet, and the prefectures of Xinjiang had not yet been opened then, and rivers and harbors still had gaps. This engraving follows the imperially commissioned compilations and fills those in, somewhat more fully than the older plate. Each square is one hundred li. The legend marks a province with ■̅, a prefecture (fu) with □, a subprefecture (ting) with ▮, a directly administered department with ⌂, a department (zhou) with ■, a county with ●, a pass with ⏠, a garrison town with ◎, and a tusi with ▲. Where the frontier marches stretch on without end, or sea and wind leave the measure unsettled, distances in li are still given and the old bearings are kept; I have not dared to alter my own view of them in the slightest. The older map was cut in stone and awkward to carry. This screen copy has been set right for viewing on the road and in lodgings, so that learned readers may hang the whole piece and look at it — that would be a kindness.
Dated the first decade of the eighth lunar month, Jiaqing 17 (rénshēn).
